subject: Geography
chapter: Planning and Sustainable Development in Indian Context
central_question: How can planning reduce regional inequality and promote development that improves present well-being without damaging ecological, social and economic prospects for future generations?
in_scope_units: Meaning of planning and the shift from the Planning Commission to NITI Aayog
Integrated Tribal Development Project in Bharmaur
Changing meaning of development and emergence of sustainable development
Brundtland Report definition of sustainable development
Indira Gandhi Canal Command Area: location, stages and transformation
Positive and negative impacts of canal irrigation
Measures for ecological, social and economic sustainability in the command area
banned_topics: General business-management planning, which is not the economic and regional planning used in this chapter
Detailed national water-resource policy, which belongs to Water Resources

known_pitfalls.claim: Sectoral planning and regional planning are identical.
known_pitfalls.correction: Sectoral planning targets economic sectors, while regional planning uses an area-specific spatial approach to reduce regional imbalance.
The chapter states that technology and investment are also necessary, so even resource-rich regions may remain backward.

known_pitfalls.claim: Development means only growth in GNP or per capita income.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter presents development as multidimensional, including equity, well-being, health, education, rights and environmental sustainability.

known_pitfalls.claim: Canal irrigation in the Indira Gandhi Canal area produced only benefits.
known_pitfalls.correction: It increased moisture, cultivated area and productivity but also caused waterlogging and soil salinity through intensive irrigation.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 1(i) to distinguish regional planning from sectoral planning.
Use NCERT Exercise 2(i) to assess the social benefits of ITDP in Bharmaur.
Use NCERT Exercise 2(ii) to state the Brundtland definition of sustainable development.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(i) to analyse the Drought Prone Area Programme.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(ii) to structure sustainability measures for the Indira Gandhi Canal Command Area.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1–3 and a PROJECT section: three MCQs, three short answers, two long answers and two field-based projects.
